rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says his treatment of the isolated letters appears at the beginning of his discussion of al-Baqarah.
rows.anchor: I have comprehensively dealt with the isolated letters

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expansive darkness is the darkness of faith and deeds; the light is faith and righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: Expansive darkness here refers to the darkness of faith and deeds and light here refers to the light of faith and righteous deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many paths lead astray while guidance has one path, which explains the plural for darkness and singular for light.
rows.anchor: For this reason, the word used for darkness occurs in the plural and that for light in the singular.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those whom God gives an urge for guidance will be brought from darkness to light; He guides the deserving and leaves those who deserve it to stray.
rows.anchor: only they will be led to light from darkness who are provided its urge from God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophet's responsibility is to communicate the message; bringing people to the path of truth is not his duty.
rows.anchor: the responsibility of the prophet is to only communicate the message

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light is the path leading to God; because He is mighty He alone is to be feared, and because He is praiseworthy He alone deserves praise and hope.
rows.anchor: The last part of the verse “to the path of the God Who is powerful; has all praiseworthy attributes” explains the word “light.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters' underlying motive is that they will not relinquish worldly interests for the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: they are not ready to give up their personal interests for the sake of the hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have turned away from God's path and try to prevent others from following it.
rows.anchor: they also try as much as they can to stop others from it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They distort the path to God toward their alleged deities, presenting these detours as routes to Him.
rows.anchor: They also try to contort the path that leads to God to take it to their alleged deities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's sending an Arab messenger and book in the Arabs' own language is a favour they should value.
rows.anchor: they should give due regard to this favour of being sent a messenger and book in their own language.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's task is to deliver the truth fully, which he has already done and continues to do.
rows.anchor: his job is to fully deliver the truth – which he has already done and is still doing.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's wise will determines who receives guidance: those who use their innate capacities receive a further urge for it, while those who neglect them lose the guidance already given.
rows.anchor: His will is governed by His wisdom. Those who deserve guidance according to His wisdom will be guided and vice versa.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham made this prayer while settling Ishmael and his mother in Makkah, which then lacked security.
rows.anchor: This supplication was made by Abraham (sws) when he was settling Ishmael (sws) and his mother in Makkah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered the prayer by making harm to animals, let alone people, a sin in Makkah.
rows.anchor: God accepted this request and even harming an animal in it was declared a sin, let alone human beings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Four months were made sacred so caravans could travel safely across Arabia; Quraysh's custody of the House gave them regional leadership and secure passage, with other tribes offering guides.
rows.anchor: In these months, caravans would be able to traverse peacefully from one part to another.

words: رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضَلَلْنَ كَثِيرًۭا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks protection from idolatry for himself and his descendants; including himself shows how great the danger of polytheism is, since many have succumbed to it.
rows.anchor: The second thing he requested in this supplication was to protect him and his progeny from the filth of idol worship.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To convey the profound influence of idols, Abraham uses nouns and pronouns conventionally used for living beings.
rows.anchor: when the purpose is to express the profundity of influence of something, the nouns and pronouns used are ones that are used for living beings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the word literally means sons, the dominant sense here is all Abraham's descendants, as confirmed by the following term for progeny.
rows.anchor: However, it is used keeping in view the dominant element.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's words leave disobedient descendants who turned to polytheism to God's judgment, with mercy for those deserving it; Islahi stresses this is no prayer on behalf of polytheists.
rows.anchor: It may be kept in mind that these words do not constitute any supplication from Abraham (sws) in favour of the polytheists.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere monotheistic worship can require leaving everything behind, even living alone in a barren land; one must never abandon God and His worship.
rows.anchor: One thing that is evident from this verse is that for monotheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The House of God is fundamentally a prayer centre, so its true custodians are those who diligently pray rather than claimants who forsake monotheism and prayer.
rows.anchor: the House of God is in reality a centre to offer the prayer.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer was the House's initial purpose; later it also became a pilgrimage centre and a place for sacrifice commemorating Ishmael's sacrifice.
rows.anchor: it also became a centre for ḥajj and also of animal sacrifice to commemorate the sacrifice of Ishmael (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression about establishing prayer includes calling people to prayer and arranging for them to perform it, not simply praying.
rows.anchor: included in it is to call people to the prayer and make arrangements for them to offer the prayer.

words: فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham first prayed that people's hearts incline toward his descendants.
rows.anchor: First, he prayed that God inclines

words: فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's prayer that people's hearts incline toward his descendants soon made the House an attraction for Arabia and, after Muhammad, virtually the world.
rows.anchor: very soon the House of God became a centre of attraction for all Arabia and after the advent of Muḥammad (sws) of virtually all the world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For barren Makkah Abraham asked for abundant provisions; it soon became Arabia's trade centre, as discussed at 2:126.
rows.anchor: The result of this prayer was that very soon it became the centre of trade in all of Arabia.

words: رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ مَا نُخْفِى وَمَا نُعْلِنُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement's eloquence lies in covering what a supplicant cannot articulate or feels shy to express, since God's knowledge includes both hidden and apparent things.
rows.anchor: This sentence has included all such things because the knowledge of God extends to all that is hidden and all that is apparent.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham recalls God's past favour of granting him two sons in old age to reinforce his hope that God will grant this new request too.
rows.anchor: in order to strengthen his supplication, Abraham (sws) has cited God’s previous favours on him.

words: رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْنِى مُقِيمَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks his descendants to carry on the prayer-centred purpose for which he built the House.
rows.anchor: he has supplicated for his progeny to fully adhere to the purpose

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “from my progeny” shows that only Ishmael, not all Abraham's descendants, was settled there.
rows.anchor: The expression “from my progeny” aptly tells us that only one part of his progeny

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the end Abraham asks God to forgive himself, his parents and all believers on the Day of Reckoning.
rows.anchor: he has supplicated to God to forgive him, his parents and all the believers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham had promised at the time of migration to seek forgiveness for his father Azar and continued doing so until God stopped him; Islahi infers this prayer probably preceded the prohibition.
rows.anchor: It seems that the supplication cited in the verse under discussion was made

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi counts Rabbi or Rabbana seven times and says the apparent repetition is essential to supplication, which repeatedly humbles itself and seeks God's attention.
rows.anchor: This apparently seems a repetition. Yet this is a feature of a supplication; in fact, it is essential.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using Rabbi presents as grounds for the plea a favour of God the supplicant has personally experienced.
rows.anchor: he wants to include as recommendation for his supplication the favour of God he has experienced.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using Rabbana presents as grounds for the plea a favour witnessed by all God's creatures.
rows.anchor: he wants to include as recommendation for his supplication

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer is retold to Quraysh so they remember why they were settled in the barren valley, recognize Abraham's prayer as the source of their blessings, and see that they wrongly credit their alleged deities.
rows.anchor: this supplication has been narrated to the Quraysh so that they recall the reason for being settled in this barren stretch of land

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing verses 42–52 assure the Prophet and threaten the disbelievers, completing the sūrah's discourse.
rows.anchor: These are the concluding verses of the sūrah in which the Prophet (sws) is assured and the disbelievers are threatened.
